title: Find a counterexample to the maximal rank conjecture.
statement:
Find a counterexample to the maximal rank conjecture.

\textbf{\emph{Conjecture}} (Maximal Rank Conjecture)

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb C$ be the annulus $A = \{1<|w| < e | w \in \mathbb C \} $. Given $(M,\omega)$ $n$-dimensional compact K\"ahler manifold, $\varphi_0$ and $\varphi_1$ potentials, the geodesic on $M \times A$ is obtained as the weak limit of solutions to the family of degenerating complex Monge-Ampère equations
\begin{cases}
(\pi^*\omega + i \partial \overline \partial \Phi_\delta)^{n+1} = \delta (\pi^*\omega + i dw\wedge d\overline w)^{n+1} \\
\Phi_\delta|_{M\times \{ 0 \} }=\varphi_0 \\
\Phi_\delta|_{M\times \{ 1 \} }=\varphi_1.
\end{cases}
Then $(\pi^*\omega+i\partial \overline \partial \Phi_\delta)|_{M\times\{\mathrm{pt.}\}} \geq \varepsilon \omega$ for $\varepsilon >0$ independent of $\delta$.
source_name: AimPL: Nonlinear PDEs in real and complex geometry (posed by Valentino Tosatti)

title: Miscellaneous (problem 5)
statement:
For $X$ and $Y$ i.i.d.\ log-concave random variables, what is

$$
\max_{\lambda \in [0,1]} h(\sqrt{\lambda} X + \sqrt{1 - \lambda} Y)?
$$

We expect that the maximum is achieved at $\lambda = 1/2$.

It is known that this is not true without log-cavity. The counterexample is given by $X,Y$ with density $x^2 \phi(x)$ where $\phi(\cdot)$ is the standard Gaussian density, which is a bi-modal density. Another counterexample exists when $X$ and $Y$ are uniform on $[a,b] \cup [-b, -a]$. For certain choices of $a$ and $b$, the maximum is achieved at $\lambda$ arbitrarily close to $0$. 

We finally note that the Shepp-Olkin conjecture is relevant here. For parameters $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n \triangleq \underline{p}$, with random variable

$$
X(\underline{p}) = Y_1 + Y_2 + \ldots + Y_n, \quad \text{ where } \quad Y_i \text{ are independent Bern}(p_i).
$$

Then $H(X(\underline{p}))$ is concave in $\underline{p}$. The open question is whether $H(X(\underline{p}))$ iincreases in $\underline{p}$ for $\underline{p} \in [0, 1/2)^n$.
source_name: AimPL: Entropy power inequalities (posed by Tomasz Tkocz)

title: Question 2.9 — Fix a basis for Fn and let An−1⊂ Aut(Fn) be the copy of Aut(Fn−1) corre- sponding to the first n− 1 basis elements.
statement: Fix a basis for Fn and let An−1⊂ Aut(Fn) be the copy of Aut(Fn−1) corre- sponding to the first n− 1 basis elements. Let φ:Aut(Fn)→G be a homomorphism of groups. If φ(An−1) is finite, must the image of φ be finite? Note that the obvious analog of this question for GL( n, Z) has a positive answer and plays a role in the foundations of algebraic K-theory. A diﬀerent approach to establishing Property (T) was developed by Zuk [ 85]. He established a combinatorial criterion on the links of vertices in a simply connected G-complex which, if satisfied, implies that G has property (T): one must show that the smallest positive eigenvalue of the discrete Laplacian on links is suﬃciently large. One might hope to apply this criterion to one of the natural complexes on which Aut( Fn) and Out( Fn) act, such as the spine of Outer space. But David Fisher has pointed out to us that the results of Izeki and Natayani [ 55] (alternatively, Schoen and Wang – unpublished) imply that such a strategy cannot succeed.
source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

title: Elliptic cohomology 4 — Yet another idea is to go back to a decription of cobordism I once heard.
statement: Yet another idea is to go back to a decription of cobordism I once heard. I think this description is in print somewhere, but I don't know where or who wrote it. I believe this idea is a geometric description of MU^* X. Think of X as a simplicial set. Over each vertex of X put a manifold. Over each edge of X put a bordism between the manifolds at the vertices. Over each triangle, put a bordism between the bordisms on the edges--I don't really know what these means, but orientation must be involved. Continue in this way, and that is an element of MU^* X. There must be some equivalence relation you put on these, but I don't know what it is. The problem would then be to figure out whether this works and if it has been published, then to determine how you get K-cohomology from this description--presumably the bordisms between bordisms go away, so are the identity, and this is the cocycle condition for vector bundles. Then figure out how to get elliptic cohomology.
source_name: Hovey's Algebraic Topology Problem List (proposed by Mark Hovey)

title: Symplectic Floer homology and Nielsen fixed point theory for mapping classes
statement:
For any mapping class $g\in\Gamma=\pi_0(\operatorname{Diff}^+(M))$, there is a monotone representative $\phi\in\operatorname{Symp}^m(M,\omega)$, with respect to some $\phi$-invariant area form $\omega$, such that
\[
HF^*(\phi)=H_*(M_{\mathrm{id}},\partial M_{\mathrm{id}};\mathbb Z_2)\oplus \mathbb Z_2^{N(\phi|_{M\setminus M_{\mathrm{id}}})},
\]
where $M_{\mathrm{id}}$ denotes the union of the components of $M\setminus\operatorname{int}(U)$ on which $\phi$ restricts to the identity. If $\psi$ is a standard Thurston-canonical-form representative of $g$ and $\lambda$ is the largest stretching factor of the pseudo-Anosov pieces of $\psi$ (with $\lambda:=1$ if there are no pseudo-Anosov pieces), then
\[
F^\infty(g):=\operatorname{Growth}\bigl(\dim HF^*(\phi^n)\bigr)=\lambda=h(\psi)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}|N(\psi^n)|^{1/n}.
\]
source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2006/33, page 27
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1319), page 27. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Gilbreath's conjecture
statement:
Let $(p_n)_{n\ge 1}=(2,3,5,7,11,13,\dots)$ be the increasing sequence of all
prime numbers, and define an array of nonnegative integers $d_n^k$ for $n\ge
1$, $k\ge 1$ by

$$
d_{n}^{k}=\begin{cases}p_{n+1}-p_{n}, & k=1,\\[5pt] \left|d_{n+1}^{k-1}-d_{n}^{k-1}\right|, & k\ge 2.\end{cases}
$$

Then $d_{1}^{k}=1$ for every $k\ge 1$.
source_name: Wikipedia
references: 1. Wikipedia, [Gilbreath's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbreath%27s_conjecture), the article this problem comes from.

title: Catalan's Mersenne conjecture
statement:
Define a sequence of integers $(c_n)_{n\ge 0}$ recursively by

$$
c_0 = 2, \qquad c_{n+1} = 2^{c_n} - 1 .
$$

Thus $c_1 = 3$, $c_2 = 7$, $c_3 = 127$,
$c_4 = 2^{127} - 1 = 170141183460469231731687303715884105727$, and
$c_5 = 2^{c_4} - 1$.

For every integer $n \ge 0$, the number $c_n$ is prime.
source_name: Wikipedia
references: 1. Wikipedia, [Double Mersenne number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_Mersenne_number), the article this problem comes from.

title: General exact upper-bound conjecture for cliques on surfaces
statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a surface with Euler characteristic $\chi$, let $\omega$ be the largest integer such that $K_\omega$ embeds in $\Sigma$, and let $G$ be a graph embeddable in $\Sigma$. Write $|V(G)|$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**General exact upper-bound conjecture.** Every graph $G$ embeddable in $\Sigma$ has at most

$$
8|V(G)|-4(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})+2^{(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})/2}
$$

cliques, with equality if and only if $K_\omega$ triangulates $\Sigma$ and $G$ is obtained from $K_\omega$ by repeatedly splitting triangles.

The preceding bound $8(|V(G)|-\omega)+2^\omega$ is reported to fail for several surfaces without complete-graph triangulations, motivating this formulation in terms of the Euler characteristic. The conjecture gives the proposed exact extremal value for all surfaces.
source_name: Vida Dujmović, Gašper Fijavž, Gwenaël Joret, Thom Sulanke and David R. Wood, “The maximum number of cliques in a graph embedded in a surface”, arXiv:0906.4142 (2011).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.4142

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2009).

title: The non-flowerable coin graph extremal equality conjecture
statement:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let a **non-flowerable collection** be a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of $n$ coins from which no flower, that is, no coin graph representation of a wheel graph, can be formed. Let $NF(\mathcal{C})$ be the maximum number of edges of a coin graph formed from coins in $\mathcal{C}$), and define

$$
NF(n)=\max\{NF(\mathcal{C}):\mathcal{C}\text{ is a non-flowerable collection of }n\text{ coins}\}.
$$

Also let $E_4(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges of a plane graph on $n$ vertices in which every vertex bounds some $\ell$-gon with $\ell\geq4$.

**Non-flowerable extremal equality conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
NF(n)=E_4(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{11}{4}n-6\right\rfloor.
$$

The source proves only the upper bound $NF(n)\leq E_4(n)$ and explicitly says that equality is unknown at the time of writing.
source_name: Geir Agnarsson and Jill Bigley Dunham, “On the maximum number of edges of non-flowerable coin graphs”, arXiv:0909.4315 (2009).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.4315

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2009). “All these slight modifications are still open problems.”

title: PageRank singular-gap conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a directed graph with $d_{min}^{out}>0$. For a parameter $\alpha$ and associated PageRank random walk, let $\mathbf{R}$ be the probability transition matrix, given by

$$
\mathbf{R}=\frac{\alpha}{n-1}(\mathbf{J}-\mathbf{I})+(1-\alpha)\mathbf{P},
$$

where $\mathbf{J}$ is the all-one matrix and $\mathbf{P}$ is the transition matrix obtained by choosing an outgoing arc uniformly at random. **PageRank singular-gap conjecture.** There is a universal constant $k$ such that

$$
\sigma_2(\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{R})^{-1}\leq \frac{k}{\alpha}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that, like the spectral gap, the PageRank parameter controls the singular gap uniformly over all directed graphs with positive minimum out-degree. The authors note that examples based on Gambler's ruin imply $k\geq 1.65637$, while the general bound remains open.
source_name: Franklin H. J. Kenter, “Concentration of the Stationary Distribution on General Random Directed Graphs”, arXiv:1309.4811 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.4811

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

title: Independence ratio conjecture for the distance graphs $\{1,6,k\}$
statement:
Let $G(S)$ be the distance graph on the integers with generating set $S$, and let $\overline{\alpha}(S)$ denote its maximum density of an independent set. Let $k>6$ with $k\notin\{7,10,12,17\}$. **The independence ratio conjecture.**

$$
\overline{\alpha}(\{1,6,k\})=
\begin{cases}
\frac{3k}{7k+7} & \text{if } k\equiv 0\pmod{7},\\
\frac{3}{7} & \text{if } k\equiv 1\pmod{7},\\
\frac{3k+1}{7k+7} & \text{if } k\equiv 2\pmod{7},\\
\frac{3k-2}{7k+7} & \text{if } k\equiv 3\pmod{7},\\
\frac{3k+2}{7k+7} & \text{if } k\equiv 4\pmod{7},\\
\frac{3k-1}{7k+7} & \text{if } k\equiv 5\pmod{7},\\
\frac{3}{7} & \text{if } k\equiv 6\pmod{7}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source notes that the proposed extremal sets are proved for all residue classes except $k\equiv3\pmod 7$, so the displayed formula remains conjectural in that class.
source_name: James M. Carraher, David Galvin, Stephen G. Hartke, A. J. Radcliff and Derrick Stolee, “On the independence ratio of distance graphs”, arXiv:1401.7183 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.7183

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

title: Häggkvist's conjecture on compatible Hamilton cycles in Dirac graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a **Dirac graph**, meaning a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $n/2$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an **incompatibility system** over $G$, consisting for each vertex $v$ of a family of unordered pairs of distinct edges incident with $v$; edges in one of these pairs are incompatible. The system is **1-bounded** if every edge incident with any vertex is incompatible with at most one other edge at that vertex. A Hamilton cycle is compatible with $\mathcal{F}$ if every pair of its edges is compatible.

**Häggkvist's conjecture.** For every 1-bounded incompatibility system $\mathcal{F}$ over a Dirac graph $G$, there exists a Hamilton cycle compatible with $\mathcal{F}$.

The paper presents this as a conjecture of Häggkvist from 1988 motivating its study. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
source_name: Michael Krivelevich, Choongbum Lee and Benny Sudakov, “Compatible Hamilton cycles in Dirac graphs”, arXiv:1410.1435 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.1435

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

title: The generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker conjecture for tilt-stable objects on threefolds
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective threefold. Let $
u_{\omega,B}$ be the tilt slope on the tilted heart $\operatorname{Coh}^{\omega,B}(X)$, where $\omega$ is ample and $B$ is a real divisor class. An object $E\in\operatorname{Coh}^{\omega,B}(X)$ is $\nu_{\omega,B}$-semistable if it satisfies the tilt-stability condition with respect to this slope. **The generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker conjecture.** For any $\nu_{\omega,B}$-semistable object $E\in\operatorname{Coh}^{\omega,B}(X)$ satisfying $\nu_{\omega,B}(E)=0$, one has

$$
\operatorname{ch}_3^B(E)\leq \frac{\omega^2}{18}\operatorname{ch}_1^B(E).
$$

This conjecture is the main inequality needed to construct Bridgeland stability conditions on threefolds. It is known in several important cases, including the abelian and Calabi–Yau threefolds of abelian type treated in the paper, but is not known for arbitrary smooth projective threefolds.
source_name: Arend Bayer, Emanuele Macrì and Paolo Stellari, “The Space of Stability Conditions on Abelian Threefolds, and on some Calabi-Yau Threefolds”, arXiv:1410.1585 (2016).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1207.4980](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.4980).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.1585

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

title: The star conjecture for minimum von Neumann entropy of connected graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices. Its scaled Laplacian is $\rho(G):=L(G)/\operatorname{tr}L(G)$, where $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, with $D(G)$ the diagonal degree matrix and $A(G)$ the adjacency matrix. The von Neumann entropy of $G$ is the Shannon entropy of the eigenvalues of $\rho(G)$, namely

$$
S(G)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i\log_2\lambda_i.
$$

Here $\{\lambda_i\}_{i=1}^n=\operatorname{spec}(\rho(G))$. **The star conjecture.** For all connected graphs on $n$ vertices, the minimum von Neumann entropy is attained by the star $K_{1,n-1}$.

This was posed because the minimum over connected graphs was open, although the extrema over all graphs were known. It was confirmed computationally through $8$ vertices, and for trees through $15$ vertices; the paper proves it for almost all graphs as $n\to\infty$, while the general connected-graph case remains open.
source_name: Michael Dairyko, Leslie Hogben, Jephian C. -H. Lin, Joshua Lockhart, David Roberson, Simone Severini and Michael Young, “Note on von Neumann and Rényi entropies of a Graph”, arXiv:1609.00420 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00420

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

title: Conjecture on the size of the minimum logarithmic derivative of Dirichlet $L$-functions
statement:
Let $q$ be an odd prime, and define

$$
m_q:=\min_{\chi \neq \chi_0 \bmod q} \Bigl\vert \frac{L'}{L}(1,\chi) \Bigr\vert.
$$

Also let

$$
Z_q:=\Bigl\{\alpha:\alpha=\frac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)\text{ for some primitive character }\chi\bmod q\Bigr\}.
$$

**Conjecture on $m_q$.** For all $\varepsilon>0$ and for all odd primes $q$,

$$
q^{-1-\varepsilon}\ll_{\varepsilon}m_q\ll_{\varepsilon}q^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.
$$

In particular, for all odd primes $q$, $0\notin Z_q$.

This conjecture is motivated by computational data for odd primes up to $10^7$, which suggest that the minimum is close to a constant multiple of $q^{-1}$. The established upper bound in the paper is weaker, of order $(\log\log q)/\sqrt{\log q}$, while the asserted lower bound would in particular imply the nonvanishing of $L'(1,\chi)$ for every nontrivial character modulo an odd prime.
source_name: Youness Lamzouri and Alessandro Languasco, “Small values of | L^/L(1,χ) |”, arXiv:2005.10714 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.10714

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

title: Conjecture on the stationary support of a quadratic Markov chain over finite fields
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with $p\equiv 1\pmod 4$. Let $\varepsilon_n$ be uniformly distributed on $\{\pm1\}$ and independent, and consider the Markov chain on $\mathbf{F}_p$ defined by

$$
X_{n+1}=X_n^2+\varepsilon_{n+1}.
$$

Write $\operatorname{supp}\pi$ for the support of a stationary distribution $\pi$, and let $\alpha\approx 0.2956$ be the smallest positive root of

$$
x^4+2x^2-4x+1=0.
$$

**Stationary-support conjecture.** Conjecturally, the chain has a unique stationary distribution $\pi$, and

$$
\frac{|\operatorname{supp}\pi|}{p}\to 1-\frac{1}{4}(1+\alpha)^2
$$

(as $p\to\infty$ through primes satisfying $p\equiv1\pmod4$). This prediction is motivated by a random directed-graph heuristic for the indegree-constrained graph associated with the chain; the conjectural limiting support proportion and uniqueness of the stationary distribution remain unproved.
source_name: Jimmy He, “Markov chains on finite fields with deterministic jumps”, arXiv:2010.10668 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.10668

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

title: Abdi–Ghorbani's uniqueness conjecture for minimum-gap quartic graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected quartic graph, meaning a $4$-regular graph, and let its spectral gap be the difference between its two largest adjacency eigenvalues. For each $n\geq 11$, let ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}$ be the specified subfamily of ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}^*$: write $n-11=5q+r$ with $q$ a non-negative integer and $0\leq r\leq 4$, take $q$ middle blocks $M$, and choose the two end blocks according to $r$ as described in the construction.

**Abdi–Ghorbani's uniqueness conjecture.** For every $n\geq11$, the $n$-vertex graph of ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}$ is the unique graph with minimum spectral gap among connected quartic graphs of order $n$.

The preceding theorem shows only that every minimum-gap connected quartic graph belongs to ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}^*$; this conjecture specifies the unique member of the smaller family ${\cal F}_{\rm qua}$ that should attain the minimum.
source_name: Maryam Abdi and Ebrahim Ghorbani, “Gap sets for the spectra of regular graphs with minimum spectral gap”, arXiv:2106.13129 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.13129

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

title: Barát–Thomassen conjecture on tree edge-decompositions
statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $G$ be a simple graph. A **$T$-edge-decomposition** is a decomposition of the edges of $G$ into isomorphic copies of $T$. The size of $G$ is $|E(G)|$, and $G$ is **$k$-edge-connected** if every nonempty proper vertex set $A$ satisfies $d_G(A)\ge k$, where $d_G(A)$ is the number of edges with exactly one end in $A$.

**Barát–Thomassen conjecture.** For every tree $T$, there exists a positive integer $k_T$ such that every $k_T$-edge-connected simple graph whose size is divisible by $|E(T)|$ admits a $T$-edge-decomposition.

This is the fundamental edge-decomposition conjecture attributed to Barát and Thomassen (2006). The paper presents stronger quantitative results for graphs with sufficiently large minimum degree, while the general assertion concerns arbitrary simple graphs and remains the motivating conjecture here.
source_name: Morteza Hasanvand, “Edge-decompositions of O(m)-edge-connected graphs into isomorphic copies of a fixed tree of size m”, arXiv:2205.10871 (2024).
references:
**8 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1611.07486](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07486), [arXiv:1603.00197](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00197), [arXiv:1603.00198](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00198), [arXiv:1509.06393](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06393), [arXiv:1507.08208](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.08208), [arXiv:1505.04309](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04309), [arXiv:1203.1671](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1671).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.10871

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

title: Genus-one STE generation conjecture for degree-15 cohomology
statement:
Let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ be the moduli space of stable curves, and let $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,11})$ and $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n})$ denote their cohomology groups. Let an **STE** mean the smallest subspace of the relevant cohomology theory closed under the constructions used in the paper, and let the STE generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,11})$ be understood accordingly. For every $g\geq 2$, **genus-one STE generation conjecture.** The STE generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,11})$ contains

$$
H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}).
$$

The preceding theorem proves the analogous containment using the generators from both $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,11})$ and $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,15})$; the conjecture asks whether the genus-one degree-11 data alone suffice for all $g\geq 2$.
source_name: Samir Canning, Hannah Larson and Sam Payne, “Extensions of tautological rings and motivic structures in the cohomology of M_g,n”, arXiv:2307.08830 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08830

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

title: Conjecture on binary Kaprekar sequences with second digits
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number written in base $2$, and let $K_{2,2}(n)$ be obtained by subtracting the second-smallest digit arrangement from the second-largest digit arrangement, retaining leading zeros. For $m\geq 3$, consider the iterates $K_{2,2}^t(n)$.

**Binary Kaprekar sequence conjecture.** $(i)$ When the digit length is $2m$, the sequence

$$
\{K_{2,2}^t(n):t=1,2,\dots\}
$$

reaches the fixed point $2^{2m}-3\times 2^m+1$. $(ii)$ When the digit length is $2m+1$, the sequence enters a loop consisting of

$$
\{2^{2m+1}-7\times 2^m+2^{m-2}+1,\,2^{2m+1}-7\times 2^m+10\times 2^{m-2}+1\}.
$$

This describes the eventual behavior of the specified binary variant of Kaprekar's routine for all digit lengths covered by the parameter range. The parser provides no evidence that the claim has been proved or disproved.
source_name: Shoei Takahashi, Unchone Lee, Hikaru Manabe, Aoi Murakami, Daisuke Minematsu, Kou Omori and Ryohei Miyadera, “Curious Properties of Iterative Sequences”, arXiv:2308.06691 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.06691

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

title: The pseudo-automorphism group conjecture for the rational threefold X
statement: Let $X$ be the rational threefold, $S$ its Jacobian Kummer surface, $R$ the unique rational normal curve through the six points blown up in constructing $X$, and $PsAut(X)$ the group of pseudo-automorphisms of $X$. Let $G$ be the subgroup generated by the $45$ Hutchinson-Göpel-type involutions and the $120$ Keum pseudo-automorphisms. **Pseudo-automorphism group conjecture.** For every $g\in PsAut(X)$, $g(R)=R$. In particular, $PsAut(X)=G$. This would fully determine the pseudo-automorphism group of $X$ by showing that every pseudo-automorphism fixes the distinguished curve $R$ and belongs to the subgroup generated by the two explicitly constructed families. The preceding results establish the structure of the subgroup $G$ and a rational polyhedral fundamental domain for its action, but the stated claim is not resolved here.
source_name: Zhuang He, “Pseudo-automorphisms of rational threefolds and Kummer surfaces”, arXiv:2401.07948 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07948

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

title: Ghosh–Győri–Paulos–Xiao conjecture on the planar Turán number of the balanced double star S_{3,3}
statement:
A **balanced double star** $S_{m,m}$ is the graph obtained from an edge whose endpoints are joined respectively to $m$ and $m$ additional distinct vertices. For a planar graph family, let $\mathrm{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,S_{3,3})$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no subgraph isomorphic to $S_{3,3}$. **Ghosh–Győri–Paulos–Xiao's conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,S_{3,3}) = \begin{cases} 3n-6 & \text{if } 3\leq n\leq 7,\\ 16 & \text{if } n=8,\\ 18 & \text{if } n=9,\\ \lfloor 5n/2\rfloor-5 & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases}
$$

This conjecture would determine the planar Turán number of the balanced double star $S_{3,3}$ for every $n$. The source reports only the bounds $\lfloor5n/2\rfloor-5\leq \mathrm{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,S_{3,3})\leq \lfloor5n/2\rfloor-2$ for $n\geq 3$, so the conjecture remains open in the supplied context.
source_name: Xin Xu, Qiang Zhou, Tong Li and Guiying Yan, “Planar Turán number for balanced double stars”, arXiv:2406.05758 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05758

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

title: Hartke's integrality gap conjecture for trees with at most 12 vertices
statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and consider the linear program obtained from the MacGillivray–Wang integer program for virus spread by relaxing $x(v)\in\{0,1\}$ to a linear constraint and adding constraint (6):

$$
\sum_{v \succeq u} x(v)+\sum_{u \succeq v,\,l(v)=i}x(v)\leq 1,
$$

for each vertex $u$ and $i>l(u)$. **Hartke's integrality gap conjecture.** The tree in Figure~ is the smallest tree such that the LP optimum under constraint (6) differs from the integer-program optimum. Equivalently, the strengthened linear program realizes the integer-program optimum for every tree with at most 12 vertices. The conjecture concerns the occurrence of integrality gaps: the displayed 13-vertex tree has LP optimum $m^*=7.5$ and integer-program optimum $m=7$, while the claim asserts that no smaller tree has such a gap.

title: Cameron's Greedy Conjecture for primitive permutation groups
statement:
Let $G\leqslant\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite permutation group. A **base** for $G$ is a sequence of points of $\Omega$ with trivial pointwise stabiliser, and $b(G)$ denotes the minimum size of a base. A **greedy base** is constructed by choosing each successive point in a longest orbit of the pointwise stabiliser of the previously chosen points; let $\mathcal{G}(G)$ be the largest size of a greedy base for $G$. **Cameron's Greedy Conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c$ such that

$$
\mathcal{G}(G)\leqslant cb(G)
$$

for every finite primitive group $G$. The conjecture would improve the general bound $\mathcal{G}(G)\leqslant db(G)\log\log|\Omega|$ to a constant-factor bound for primitive groups; it was proposed by Cameron in 1999 and its status is not resolved by the supplied source.
source_name: Hong Yi Huang and Colva M. Roney-Dougal, “Greedy bases and relational complexity of diagonal type groups”, arXiv:2605.16032 (2026).
references:

title: Balogh–Lidický–Mubayi–Pfender–Volec lower-profile conjecture for the red-blue star
statement:
Let $S_{2,1}$ be the red-blue star with one distinguished centre, two ordered red leaves, and one blue leaf, and let $i(S_{2,1},\beta)$ denote its fixed-density lower profile. The quasi-star and quasi-clique are the two endpoint constructions referred to in the source.

**Balogh–Lidický–Mubayi–Pfender–Volec's lower-profile conjecture.** For every $\beta\in[0,1]$,

$$
i(S_{2,1},\beta)=\begin{cases}(1-\beta)(1-\sqrt{1-\beta})^2,&0\leq\beta\leq x,\\[1mm]\beta^{3/2}(1-\sqrt{\beta}),&x\leq\beta\leq 1,\end{cases}
$$

where $x\in(0,1)$ is a solution to

$$
(1-\beta)(1-\sqrt{1-\beta})^2=\beta^{3/2}(1-\sqrt{\beta}),
$$

i.e. $16x^3-40x^2+41x-16=0$.

This conjecture asserts that the minimum is attained by the quasi-star and quasi-clique endpoint constructions. The supplied text gives no resolution status for this lower-profile claim.
source_name: Jinghua Deng and Jianfeng Hou, “Fixed-density profiles for the semi-induced 4-vertex star”, arXiv:2606.23351 (2026).

title: Cyclic interval conjecture for odd cycles
statement:
Let $m$ be odd and let $x\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_m$ with $x\notin\{\emptyset,\mathbb{Z}_m\}$. An **arc** $W$ is a cyclic interval in $\mathbb{Z}_m$. Write $C_m$ for the cycle graph on $m$ vertices, and let $k_{\min}(C_m)$ denote the minimum dimension of an isometric embedding of $C_m$ into an abelian group. The lemma asserts that there is an arc $W$ satisfying

$$
|W\triangle x|<\min(|W|,m-|W|).
$$

**Cyclic interval conjecture.** The displayed inequality holds for every odd $m$ and every nonempty proper subset $x\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_m$; consequently,

$$
k_{\min}(C_m)=m-1
$$

for every odd cycle $C_m$.

The inequality is the remaining case beyond the covering-arc regime and has been verified exhaustively for all odd $m\leq 17$. If true, it gives the naive-dimension lower bound for every odd cycle; the general case remains open.
source_name: Fokam Souop Rigobert and Bitjoka Laurent, “Minimal Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Abelian Groups: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications to Signal Processing over Networks”, arXiv:2606.29391 (2026).

title: The ideal neoplatonic conjecture
statement:
A **6-net** is a simplicial triangulation of the $2$-sphere with maximum degree at most $6$. A net is **prime** if every $3$-cycle bounds a face. An **ideal neoplatonic** is an equilateral ideal hyperbolic polyhedron whose ideal triangular faces meet midpoint-to-midpoint, where the midpoint of an infinite edge is the foot of the perpendicular dropped from the opposite vertex. For a $6$-net $\sigma$, write $\Delta(\sigma,\infty)$ for its ideal realization.

**Ideal neoplatonic conjecture.** Every $6$-net $\sigma$ has a realization $\Delta(\sigma,\infty)$, unique up to isometry, as an ideal neoplatonic.

The conjecture proposes existence and uniqueness for all $6$-nets. The source proves a convex ideal neoplatonic realization, unique up to isometry, for every prime $6$-net with at most $50$ vertices, but does not establish the general assertion.

title: The minimum-degree conjecture for colour-biased loose Hamilton cycles
statement:
Let $H$ be a red/blue coloured $3$-graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta_1(H)$ denote its minimum vertex degree. A **loose Hamilton cycle** is a cyclic ordering of the vertices in which every consecutive block of three vertices beginning at positions congruent to $1$ modulo $2$ forms an edge; it has $n/2$ edges. **The minimum-degree conjecture for colour-biased loose Hamilton cycles.** For every $\alpha>0$, there exist $\delta,n_0>0$ such that, whenever $n\geq n_0$ and

$$
\delta_1(H)\geq \left(\frac{7}{16}+\alpha\right)\binom{n}{2},
$$

$H$ contains a loose Hamilton cycle with at least $(\frac{1}{4}+\delta)n$ edges of the same colour. This is proposed as the colour-biased analogue of the known asymptotically sharp minimum vertex-degree threshold $\frac{7}{16}\binom{n}{2}$ for loose Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs; the source gives no resolution.
source_name: Natalie Behague, Felix Christian Clemen, Joseph Hyde and Natasha Morrison, “A minimum-degree threshold for colour-biased Hamilton cycles in hypergraphs”, arXiv:2607.29628 (2026).

title: Regular-graph reformulation of Boesch's maximum-girth conjecture
statement:
Let a **uniformly most reliable graph (UMRG)** be a graph with the highest all-terminal reliability among graphs having the same order and size, for every edge-failure probability. For a graph, the **girth** $g$ is the length of its shortest cycle, and a $k$-regular graph has every vertex of degree $k$.

**Regular Boesch conjecture.** If an $(n,kn/2)$ UMRG exists and has girth $g$, then it has maximum girth among all $k$-regular $(n,kn/2)$-graphs and, among the $k$-regular $(n,kn/2)$-graphs with girth $g$, it has the minimum number of $g$-cycles.

This is presented as a reformulation of Boesch's maximum-girth conjecture. The supplied text does not give a separate resolution of this reformulation; the broader maximum-girth claim is nevertheless refuted by the reported 4-regular $(9,18)$ UMRG of girth $3$.
source_name: Nicole Rosenstock and Eduardo A. Canale, “Counterexample to a Boesch's Conjecture”, arXiv:2212.03912 (2022).

title: Gray–Wyner conjecture for the doubly symmetric binary source
statement:
Let $(X,Y)$ be a doubly symmetric binary source ${\mathrm{DSBS}}(p)$ with $p\in(0,1/2)$. Let $R(D_{1},D_{2})$ denote its rate-distortion function under Hamming distortion, let $h$ be the binary entropy function, and let $R_{0}(R_{1},R_{2})$ be the minimum common rate in the Gray–Wyner coding system when the private rates are $(R_{1},R_{2})$. **Gray–Wyner conjecture.** For every $(R_{1},R_{2})\in[0,1]^{2}$,

$$
R_{0}(R_{1},R_{2})=R(h^{-1}(R_{1}),h^{-1}(R_{2})).
$$

Equivalently, the layered coding scheme that first uses an optimal point-to-point lossy compression code with distortions $(D_{1},D_{2})$ and then losslessly compresses the residuals at rates $h(D_{1})$ and $h(D_{2})$ should be optimal for the Gray–Wyner system for the DSBS. The conjecture has been open since 1974, with the source stating that no progress had been made on it at the time of publication.
source_name: Lei Yu, “Gray–Wyner and Mutual Information Regions for Doubly Symmetric Binary Sources and Gaussian Sources”, arXiv:2212.14696 (2023).
references:

title: Saito’s conjecture on positivity of eta products for integers with at least two distinct prime divisors
statement:
For every positive integer $h$ divisible by at least two distinct primes, all Fourier coefficients in the $q$-expansion of
$$
\eta(h\tau)^{\phi(h)}\prod_{d\mid h}\eta(d\tau)^{\mu(d)}
$$
are non-negative, where $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$ with $\operatorname{Im}(\tau)>0$, $\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}(1-q^n)$, $\phi$ is Euler’s totient function, and $\mu$ is the Möbius function.

\]
have to be non-negative? Here $\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)$ with $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, and $\varphi$ and $\mu$ denote the Euler and Möbius functions, respectively.

title: Nonvanishing Hankel determinants for a morphic sequence
